source.name: sp_SharedTempReport

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_SharedTempReport()
RETURNS TABLE (
    OrderDate DATE,
    TotalOrders INT,
    TotalRevenue DECIMAL(12,2)
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- PostgreSQL uses local temporary tables instead of global temp tables
    -- The temp table is automatically dropped at end of session/transaction
    CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS temp_global_order_summary (
        OrderDate DATE,
        TotalOrders INT,
        TotalRevenue DECIMAL(12,2)
    ) ON COMMIT DROP;

    -- Clear any existing data if table already exists
    DELETE FROM temp_global_order_summary;

    INSERT INTO temp_global_order_summary
    SELECT
        CAST(OrderDate AS DATE),
        COUNT(*)::INT,
        SUM(TotalAmount)
    FROM dbo.Orders
    GROUP BY CAST(OrderDate AS DATE);

    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        t.OrderDate,
        t.TotalOrders,
        t.TotalRevenue
    FROM temp_global_order_summary t
    ORDER BY t.OrderDate DESC;

    -- Temp table will be dropped automatically due to ON COMMIT DROP
END;
$$;
assumptions: The global temporary table ##GlobalOrderSummary is converted to a local temporary table since PostgreSQL does not have true global temporary tables
The procedure returns a result set, so it is converted to a FUNCTION returning TABLE
SET NOCOUNT ON is omitted as PostgreSQL functions don't send row count messages by default
The dbo schema exists in the target PostgreSQL database
The Orders table structure is compatible with the query (has OrderDate and TotalAmount columns)
ON COMMIT DROP is used to automatically clean up the temp table after the transaction
COUNT(*) is explicitly cast to INT to match the return type

reviewFlags.reason: Global temp tables (##) in SQL Server are visible across sessions. PostgreSQL temp tables are session-local only. If cross-session visibility is required, consider using a permanent application table with session tracking or advisory locks.
reviewFlags.codeSection: CREATE TEMP TABLE IF NOT EXISTS temp_global_order_summary

reviewFlags.reason: Verify that the dbo schema and Orders table exist in PostgreSQL with the same structure (OrderDate and TotalAmount columns)
The calling application must be updated to handle this as a function call (SELECT * FROM dbo.sp_SharedTempReport()) rather than EXEC dbo.sp_SharedTempReport
The temp table will be dropped at transaction end. If the function is called multiple times in the same transaction, verify this behavior meets requirements

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's ##GlobalOrderSummary is visible across all sessions until explicitly dropped or server restart. PostgreSQL temp tables are session-scoped only and not visible to other sessions. This changes the semantics significantly if cross-session access was intended.
The stored procedure is converted to a function returning a table. Calling syntax changes from EXEC/EXECUTE to SELECT * FROM function_name(). Client code must be updated accordingly.

PostgreSQL temp tables with ON COMMIT DROP are automatically cleaned up at transaction end. The explicit DROP TABLE statement is no longer needed but the cleanup timing may differ from SQL Server's explicit DROP.
PostgreSQL functions do not send row count messages by default, so this setting is not needed and has no equivalent.
